title: Major Non-NATO Ally Terror Threat Assessment Act
official_title: To require an assessment of terrorism threats to the United States posed by foreign terrorist organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists present in countries that are major non-NATO allies, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: House passage recorded July 13, 2026 per the latest action. Sponsored by a Republican member with one cosponsor; referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security. The measure now moves to the Senate.
summary: Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence, to submit to the appropriate congressional committees an assessment of terrorism threats to the United States posed by foreign terrorist organizations (FTOs) and Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs) present in countries that are operating or designated as major non-NATO allies (MNNAs). The first assessment is due within 180 days after enactment; biennial assessments follow. Each assessment must identify each FTO or SDGT present in each MNNA; describe their activities within each ally (including use of artificial intelligence or critical and emerging technologies); describe the MNNA government's efforts to disrupt and degrade those activities and any cooperation with elements of the U.S. intelligence community; assess DHS's capability to identify, monitor, and mitigate the threats and to prevent members from entering the United States; and identify any additional resources required. Assessments are submitted in classified form and made available to every Member of Congress upon request; each assessment is followed by a congressional briefing. Definitions incorporate: "artificial intelligence" (section 5002 of the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020, 15 U.S.C. 9401), "critical and emerging technologies" (the February 2024 Critical and Emerging Technologies List Update issued by NSTC, or any successor), "intelligence community" (section 3(4) of the National Security Act of 1947, 50 U.S.C. 3003(4)), "foreign terrorist organization" (section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, 8 U.S.C. 1189), "major non-NATO ally" (section 644 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, 22 U.S.C. 2403), "specially designated global terrorist" (per Executive Order 13224, September 23, 2001; 66 Fed. Reg. 49079), and "terrorism" (section 2 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, 6 U.S.C. 101).
brief: Directs DHS, in consultation with State and ODNI, to submit a classified biennial assessment (first due 180 days after enactment) of FTO and SDGT presence and activity in major non-NATO ally countries — including use of AI and critical and emerging technologies — plus a congressional briefing on each.

items.main: Names the Act the "Major Non-NATO Ally Terror Threat Assessment Act."
items.detail: Short-title section only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Assessment of Terrorism Threats to the United States by FTOs and SDGTs Present in Countries That Are Major Non-NATO Allies

items.main: Not later than 180 days after enactment and biennially thereafter, the Secretary of Homeland Security — in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence — must submit an assessment of terrorism threats to the United States posed by FTOs and SDGTs present in countries operating or designated as major non-NATO allies.
items.detail: Subsection (a) sets the recurring assessment requirement.

items.main: Each assessment must, for each MNNA: identify each FTO or SDGT present; describe all activities each identified group or individual is engaged in within that ally, including the extent to which they are using artificial intelligence or critical and emerging technologies; describe the government of each MNNA's disruption and degradation efforts, including cooperation with U.S. intelligence community elements; assess DHS's capability to identify, monitor, and mitigate the threats; assess DHS's capability to prevent identified members from entering the United States; and identify any additional resources required to counter the threats.
items.detail: Subsection (b) enumerates six required elements for each MNNA.

items.main: Each assessment is submitted in classified form and made available to every Member of Congress upon request. The Secretary must provide a congressional briefing on each assessment upon submission.
items.detail: Subsections (c) and (d) set form/availability and briefing requirements.

items.main: Definitions in subsection (e) tie all key terms to existing statutes and issuances: "artificial intelligence" to 15 U.S.C. 9401; "critical and emerging technologies" to the February 2024 NSTC list; "intelligence community" to 50 U.S.C. 3003(4); "foreign terrorist organization" to 8 U.S.C. 1189; "major non-NATO ally" to 22 U.S.C. 2403; "specially designated global terrorist" to Executive Order 13224; and "terrorism" to 6 U.S.C. 101.
items.detail: Definitions rely on incorporated cross-references rather than newly created terms.

gaps: The bill does not identify which countries currently qualify as major non-NATO allies — that list is maintained under other law and would need to be consulted separately.
The bill does not authorize additional funding to carry out the assessment or briefing requirements.
The bill does not specify consequences if the Secretary misses the 180-day or biennial deadline.
The bill does not require a public or unclassified summary of the assessment.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Van Epps
featured_quotes.text: When the United States designates a nation as a major non-NATO ally, MNNA, it comes with security cooperation and possible trade deals for defense equipment. This is an important designation that our Nation does not grant lightly. However, we cannot ignore the fact that foreign terrorist organizations continue to operate in or around some MNNA countries, creating threats that could have serious consequences for U.S. national security.

added: 180-day and biennial classified DHS assessment of FTO and SDGT activity in major non-NATO allies
Requirement to describe use of artificial intelligence and critical and emerging technologies by identified FTOs/SDGTs
Requirement to assess DHS capability to identify, monitor, and mitigate the threats, and to prevent identified members from entering the United States
Congressional briefing on each assessment upon submission
Any-Member-upon-request availability of the classified assessment
